text:
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] Canary latency spike detected for model opt-1.2-qat on canary pool canary-eu-west-1-1. p95=820ms (SLO 500ms), p99=2600ms (SLO 1000ms). Streaming stall rate up 18%. Paging oncall.

oncall-mike: acked, I'm on it. grabbing edge metrics and recent deploy logs.

anika: copying — we pushed opt-1.2-qat to canary ~09:05 UTC, 10% traffic. Any config changes?

sara: no infra config changes. runtime flags for continuous batching were turned on in the model profile for opt-1.2-qat (batching=adaptive, max_batch=64).

oncall-mike: seeing a spike in tail latencies correlated with high kv-cache miss rate on the canary layer. dumping logs now.

infra-bot: recent events for canary-eu-west-1-1:
```
2026-03-14T09:14:22Z canary-eu-west-1-1 deploy:opt-1.2-qat request_id=ab12 latency_ms=2620 stream_stall=true kv_cache_miss=true batch_size=48
2026-03-14T09:14:23Z canary-eu-west-1-1 runtime:batch_queue_length=27 active_gpus=4
2026-03-14T09:14:25Z canary-eu-west-1-1 kernel_warn:quant-path-fallback=true
```

dmitri: looks like quantization kernel fallback plus big batches. If kernels fallback we can hit huge tail. Could be model_variant mismatch with compiled kernels.

oncall-mike: hypothesis: opt-1.2-qat's new attention kernel combo + adaptive batching is causing periodic long tail when cache misses coincide with large batches. Streaming stalls likely due to blocking on KV fetch.

anika: customers on canary list? cust-success-jen, any customer reports?

cust-success-jen: yes — 3 tickets from EU customers about streaming stalls and slow completions since ~09:12 UTC. Two of them are degraded but still responding (long delays), one timed out and retried. I'm flagging impacted accounts for postmortem.

sara: we should reduce canary traffic immediately and consider rollback. Options: 1) throttle canary to 0% via routing policy, 2) scale up canary pool GPUs temporarily, 3) roll back to opt-1.1. Which gives fastest mitigation?

oncall-mike: fastest is cut traffic to 0% (console toggle) and rollback. Scaling helps but takes time. I'll cut traffic now.

oncall-mike: /run: rtr set-weight canary-eu-west-1-1 opt-1.2-qat 0% --reason "latency spike"

infra-bot: routing change applied, canary traffic set to 0% at 1769010105.

dmitri: initiating rollback — preparing opt-1.1 canary pod template. Note: opt-1.1 uses compiled kernels we trust.

anika: if we rollback, ensure model version pinning and cache warmup steps (set fast-warmup=true) to avoid initial cold tail.

oncall-mike: starting rollback via deploy API now.

infra-bot: rollback job started: deploy.rollback id=job-8842 -> target opt-1.1, canary-eu-west-1-1.

sara: I'll watch metrics. Can you also temporarily decrease max_batch to 16 for canary runtime to reduce amplification while rollback completes?

oncall-mike: applying runtime patch:
```
patch runtime canary-eu-west-1-1 --set max_batch=16 --set adaptive_batching=false
```

infra-bot: runtime patch applied at 1769010280.

anika: rollback completed at 1769010402 and healthchecks passed. Confirming model id now opt-1.1 on canary.

oncall-mike: metrics update: new p95=340ms, p99=720ms, streaming stall rate dropped to 1.4%. Still above ideal but within acceptable for now.

cust-success-jen: informed impacted customers that we rolled back the canary and are monitoring; offering support. No escalations to legal/enterprise yet.

dmitri: I'll take ownership for the 1h handoff to watch for recurrence. oncall-mike handing off. @oncall-mike over to you for final notes?

oncall-mike: handing off to dmitri. Summary: cause likely kernel fallback + large adaptive batching on opt-1.2-qat causing blocking on KV cache misses -> tail latency + streaming stalls. Mitigations: routed canary traffic to 0%, runtime patch to reduce batch amplification, rollback to opt-1.1. Customer impact: a handful of streaming stalls, one retry/timeouts reported.

incident-bot: INVESTIGATION UPDATE: canary rollback done, mitigations applied. Current state: degraded -> recovering.

dmitri: adding next steps: 1) model artifact validation: ensure kernel compatibility matrix capture for new model variants, 2) add preflight that checks quant-kernel availability on canary hardware, 3) add synthetic streaming load during canary rollout to catch stalls, 4) follow up postmortem and customer impact assessment.

anika: noted. I'll file a postmortem and schedule a model-onboarding check in the pipeline.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED at 1769010680 — canary traffic restored to controlled levels with opt-1.1. Please add any follow-ups to the incident ticket #INC-2026-045. :white_check_mark:

cust-success-jen: closing loop with customers, will attach incident summary when ready.

dmitri: thanks all.
